scope: CC0 real-game KPK development continuation and constructed controls. Full engine estimates are distinct from the exact king-and-pawn outcome proof; no general classifier accuracy estimate.
humanReview: The real Kf4 move forces a winning pawn-ending transition after every defence; it does not already create the later KPK zugzwang. Kf3 at ply five is the separate opposition lesson.
The missed Kd3 continuation evaluates near a draw. The hypothetical pass also evaluates near a draw. Exact table outcomes, not these centipawn thresholds, admit zugzwang.

In the constructed defensive mistake, Kc6 holds while Kd6 loses. Stockfish prefers White Kb5 after Kd6; the teaching Kd4 is another table-confirmed winning continuation, not a claim that it is the first engine PV.
The real earlier pawn ending is already lost after both Kf5 and Kf6, so the opponent's later zugzwang is not blamed on that choice.
Guarded-pawn, rook-pawn and promotion-escape controls reject the four-piece entry proof. A position won with either side to move is not labelled zugzwang.

The three larger-pawn king retreats remain losing in the fresh engine searches, but material exchanges and cross-wing counterplay defeat the attempted local proof. That experimental verifier was withdrawn; the larger zugzwang remains unclassified.
